method: Read-based reconciliation of repeated constructions; occurrence records remain distinct where the source changes hypotheses, status, or purpose.

families.relationship: The later Galois-connection formulation restates and generalizes the early two-pair notation. The closure and polarity subclaims are recorded separately, not counted as new discoveries.
Different uses of the same arrow-retract mechanism: generated trivial-class identities, recognition of a WFS, and recognition of prescribed W.

Early factorization is admitted; the all-squares set-generated construction is later sketched and made functorial; the mono/injective factorization is a separate topos application; removal of set generation remains an explicit next step.
Recognition of a prescribed W is distinct from existence of some accessible-localizer model structure or from the existence of factorizations.
Mild, cyclic, retract and strong saturation hypotheses must remain separate.
The valid continuous-ordinal closure is a narrowing of the unfinished arbitrary-directed argument, not its proof.
Absolute weak equivalence of a replacement, pointwise Kan calculation, coherent square construction and coefficient transport are distinct steps.
Conditional exactness, proposed stable square axioms, the expressly withdrawn unstable claims and the third cube implication have different statuses.
Opposite-edge and cube axioms, and their smooth/proper variants, are retained separately with cross-referenced counterexamples.
